# Weekly Blog Writeup

Draft the weekly Substack recap for the agentic fantasy football experiment. This is research plus a blog draft. Do not change rosters, file waivers, or tell the league agents what to do.

Fill [assets/template.md](assets/template.md). That file is the shape. The posts in `references/` and on https://indefinitec.substack.com are the voice. Casey will edit the draft, so get the facts right and leave the voice a little loose rather than polished and generic.

## Where the data lives

Base URL: `https://leagueapi.caseyk.dev`

Season is whatever `GET /api/league/state` says. Do not hardcode it.

| What | Endpoint | Use it for |
|------|----------|------------|
| League clock | `GET /api/league/state` | Current season, week, and phase. If the week has already advanced, current roster slots are not the completed week's lineup. |
| Scores | `GET /api/league/seasons/{season}/schedule/{week}` | Matchups, points, winner. These totals are authoritative. |
| Next week | `GET /api/league/seasons/{season}/schedule/{week+1}` | The closer. |
| Standings | `GET /api/league/seasons/{season}/standings` | Record and points for. |
| Names and models | `GET /api/agent-profiles?enabledOnly=false` | Team name and `modelName`. Do not invent either. |
| Decision logs | `GET /api/decisions?week={week}&limit=200` | Why they started, sat, added, or passed. Also pull `week-1` if a running joke needs the callback, and `week+1` if the waiver window is already open. |
| One agent's log | `GET /api/decisions/{agentId}` | Use if the week query is truncated. The list endpoint caps at 200. |
| Rosters | `GET /api/rosters/{agentId}` | Names, positions, projections, ranks, injury/status, and `weeklyPoints`. |
| Waivers that affected this week | `GET /api/league/waivers/{season}/{week}` | Claims filed before this week's games. |
| Waivers already filed for next week | `GET /api/league/waivers/{season}/{nextWeek}` and `GET /api/league/waivers/priority` | Only if the league has moved into the next waiver window. |
| Player lookup | `GET /api/players/{sleeperPlayerId}` | Turn a waiver add/drop id into a name, and check projection/rank when a sit looks insane. |

Known agent ids: `anthropic`, `google`, `inception`, `meta`, `mistralai`, `nvidia`, `openai`, `poolside`, `thinkingmachines`, `xai`. Confirm against profiles. Team names are generated by the agents and can change; the profile endpoint wins.

Scoring is full PPR. Report points to one decimal. Drop a trailing `.0` only when it reads cleaner (`180`, not `180.0`).

## Research order

1. Fetch the completed week's schedule, league state, profiles, and standings.
2. Read `references/week1.md` and `references/week2.md` for voice. Then fetch `https://indefinitec.substack.com/feed` and read any weekly post that is not already in `references/`, especially last week's, for callbacks. Shape comes from the template, not from those posts.
3. Download every decision for that week and every roster. Save them locally if the payloads are large. Do not try to hold raw JSON in your head.
4. Reconstruct the lineup that actually scored. See below. Do this before writing a single matchup.
5. Verify each reconstructed lineup's starter points sum to that side's matchup total. If they do not match, stop and fix the reconstruction. Do not publish a story on a lineup that does not add up.
6. Read the decisions that changed the lineup, not just the Monday "everything is locked" note.
7. When a bench player crushed a starter, check projection and rank before calling it stupid. Sometimes the agent followed the catalog and the player just had a day. Sometimes the catalog does not say what the agent claims it says.
8. Read the weekly reflections last. They are useful for what the agent thinks it learned. They are not the box score. Agents rewrite history. If the reflection disagrees with the decision log or the points, trust the log and the points, and say so.
9. Check waiver claims for this week and, if the phase is already `waiver_window`, claims already filed for next week.
10. Pull next week's schedule for the closer.

Web search is optional color (a real injury, a real "ruled out" that the agent invented). It is never the source of fantasy points.

## Reconstructing the lineup

This is the step that goes wrong.

`GET /api/rosters/{agentId}` is the roster **right now**. `slotType` and `isStarter` are the current slots. When this skill is run the league state has already moved to the next week, those slots are next week's lineup, or a half-edited one. Do not treat them as the completed week's starters.

The lineup that scored is in the decision log:

- Find that agent's `Roster Management` decisions for the week, ordered by `createdAtUtc`.
- The last decision that still lists a `Starting lineup` while games are locked (usually Sunday night or Monday) is the lineup that scored.
- Earlier decisions are where the start/sit actually happened. Read those for the quote. Thursday and Saturday runs often set the lineup. Monday runs usually say `no_change` because everyone is locked.
- Join starter names to `weeklyPoints["{week}"]` on the roster. Bench points come from the same map.
- Starters are QB1, RB1, RB2, WR1, WR2, TE1, FLEX1, K1, DEF1. Defense and kicker count.

A player can be `Out` or `IR` in the current roster and still have been started. A player can also have points while marked Out if the status flipped after they played. Say what the log said at the time, and what the points were. Do not smooth that into one clean sentence if the two disagree.

## What to look for

Write about decisions, not just box scores. A 40-point win with no choice in it is a short section. A 6-point game that turned on one sit is the post.

Look for:

- **The swing.** A bench player at the same position outscored the starter. Do the math. Only say it cost them the game if the difference is bigger than the margin. If they still lose, say that. "The miss was real and also irrelevant" is a fine sentence.
- **Process vs outcome.** A cautious sit can be reasonable and still be wrong. A reckless sit can win the week. Separate those. Quantum sitting a questionable star and writing down the risk is a different story from an agent claiming the catalog ranks a bench player higher when it does not.
- **Hallucinations and stale notes.** An agent decides a healthy player is OUT, PUP, or ruled out, then the roster data or a later log contradicts it. Quote both. Week 1 was Christian Watson on a fake PUP. Week 3 was CeeDee Lamb "ruled out" while the roster said Active, then locked on the bench after he played.
- **Recap vs box score.** The weekly reflection sometimes lists a benched player as a start, or calls a fill-in "validated" when the star played. That is part of the story.
- **Adds that mattered.** Waiver claims and free-agent adds during the week. Did the add start? What did they score? What got dropped? Resolve ids through `/api/players/{id}`.
- **The one correct ugly decision.** Starting the boring higher-ranked player who then scored 4, while the bench scored 30, is not automatically a mistake. Say when they followed rank and got unlucky.
- **Continuity.** Callbacks the series already set up. Did they start the guy they sat last week? Did they repeat the tight-end mistake and get the opposite result? Read the prior post or the prior week's decisions before inventing a callback.
- **What they have not fixed yet.** If the reflection calls a benching a critical miss and the current roster still has that player on the bench, say so. That is the next-week hook.

Do not invent Casey's personal fantasy team, his feelings about a player, or a joke he did not make. The week 1 post has personal asides. Leave a blank beat if one would help, or skip it. He will add those.

Do not treat one big week as proof a process is broken, and do not treat one quiet week from a star as a drop candidate. The agents' own logs often say this. Agree with them when the points support it.

## How to read a decision

Each decision has `type`, `action`, `reasoning`, and `createdAtUtc`.

- `Roster Management` with outcome `changed` or `added` is a move. Pull the `Changes` lines and the one sentence of `Why` that is actually the reason.
- `no_change` on Monday is confirmation of the locked lineup, not a decision.
- Waiver attempts are usually the first run of the week. `Successful` is not the same as "they started him."
- Free-agent adds midweek show up as `added` during `free_agency`, not only in the waiver endpoint.
- Quote the log when the wording is the joke or the indictment. Keep quotes short. Do not paste the whole reasoning block into the post.

If the justification cites `projectedFantasyPoints` or rank, check those fields on the roster before repeating the claim.

## Draft

Write the draft in the chat. Do not publish it. Do not leave it in the repo unless Casey asks.

The output contract is [assets/template.md](assets/template.md). Read it and fill every placeholder. Start the draft at the H1. Strip every HTML comment. Do not copy instruction text, sample labels, or unfilled braces into the post.

Section order comes from the template, not from older posts. Week 1 and week 2 were written before this template. Week 3 on Substack was drafted in the old shape. Do not copy those outlines.

Voice comes from the saved posts:

- [references/week1.md](references/week1.md) — [week 1](https://indefinitec.substack.com/p/the-agentic-fantasy-football-experiment-94c)
- [references/week2.md](references/week2.md) — [week 2](https://indefinitec.substack.com/p/the-agentic-fantasy-football-experiment-bb4)

Read both before writing. Match the tone: specific, a little loose, funny when the log is funny.

Continuity comes from the live blog, not only from those two files. Fetch `https://indefinitec.substack.com/feed` and read any league post that is not already in `references/`, especially the previous week. Use it for callbacks and for questions the last post already asked. Do not repeat a joke or a storyline that already ran. If a local file and the live post disagree about what readers saw, trust the live post.

Use the team name from profiles, not the agent id, in the prose. Put the agent id and model in the matchup headline the way the examples do: `Neural Endzone (anthropic/claude-sonnet-5)`. Shorten a model slug only if an earlier post already established the short form. Otherwise use `modelName` from the profile.

Do not invent Casey's personal fantasy team, his feelings about a player, or a joke he did not make. The examples have personal asides. Leave a blank beat if one would help, or skip it. He will add those.

## Checks before you send the draft

- Every score matches the schedule endpoint.
- Every starter line sums to that score.
- Every "this cost them the game" claim survives the margin math.
- Every quote is from a decision log, not from a reflection you paraphrased into a quote.
- No current-week slot is described as last week's starter unless you confirmed it in the locked lineup.
- Team names and models came from profiles.
- You did not file a waiver, move a player, or edit league state.
- The draft has no HTML comments, no `{placeholders}`, and no instruction sentences left in from the template.
- Section order matches the template, including the scores table and the standings table.
